hypothesis: Bare fails because of bookkeeping, not because it lacks queries: the 7B sweeps rows exhaustively and then mis-transcribes even rows it queried (i105 A fully queried and still wrong; on i11/i164/i98 bare's own 18 answers already pin down all three circuits under the rules, yet it scored 0/3). If the harness enumerates the rule-derived circuit space (3 inputs, exactly two binary gates per circuit, NOTs anywhere, no constant circuit, inventory used exactly, joint across A/B/C), shows the model which rows are still uncertain and which split best, vetoes zero-information queries, and has the model copy determined tables one line per circuit, then exact-table accuracy on this batch rises from 0/10 to >=9/10 using <18 queries. Falsified if exact accuracy stays below 9/10 or if the final tables only come out right because the harness overwrites the model's tables.
behavior_changes: Harness enumerates every 3-input circuit table allowed by the system-prompt rules and the inventory (per-circuit gate split enumerated jointly), filtered by all answers so far; marginals per circuit.

Each turn the model gets a fresh compact prompt (system prompt + state) instead of the growing transcript: answers per circuit, rows already implied (marked as wasted), still-uncertain rows, and up to 4 queries that split the remaining candidates most evenly.

Queries on answered or already-implied rows are vetoed with a reason and the model is re-asked (max 4 asks per turn, 6*budget calls total); a single untagged X(a,b,c) mention is accepted as the query.
Querying stops early once all three circuits are determined.

Final turn: the model sees all answers plus each circuit's determined table (or its remaining consistent tables), writes one 'A: <8 digits>' line per circuit and the 24-digit guess; harness parses per-circuit lines first (24-digit guess as fallback), snaps each circuit to the consistent table nearest to what the model wrote, and returns only <guess>...</guess>.
preserved_behaviors: Frozen solver: only self.llm is called; the model writes every query sent to env.query and the final tables.
Label-free: knowledge comes only from env.system_prompt rules, env.inventory and env.history; audit.py --arm scratch reports OK.
Benchmark system prompt and last-turn prompt are still sent verbatim; budget respected (never exceeds env.remaining).
verification: Offline: all 10 bare histories are consistent with the rule-derived space (no empty marginals). Simulating a best-split chooser on random hypotheses from the space determined all circuits within 18 queries (max 11 / 15 / 17 for the three inventory types).

check script v1: 10/10 exact, 3/3 circuits each, 6-15 queries, 0 crashes. Trace audit: model picked the top-ranked menu query often, other menu entries and off-menu queries regularly (it is choosing); 1 veto (i250). On i156 the model dropped 2 digits concatenating 24 bits twice; the fallback rescued it.
v2 (per-circuit lines): still 10/10, but on i128 the model copied my example digits into the A/B lines and only the snap rescued it -- a prompt bug.

v3 (placeholder example, final): 10/10 exact, 0 crashes, queries 6-15 (mean 10.9 vs 17.7 bare), one final call per instance, and on all 10 the model's own per-circuit lines equal the returned table, so the snap altered nothing; outcome is not produced by harness override.
No sibling-branch traces existed in traces/b0 (only bare), so there were no cross-branch disagreements to adjudicate; claims are judged against bare traces and the re-runs.
risks: Query choice is heavily guided: the model mostly follows the ranked menu, so success depends on the harness's split ranking; a stricter reading of 'the model must choose' could consider the menu too directive.

The hypothesis space is my reading of the rules (two binary gates per circuit, stacked NOTs allowed). If the generator allows structures outside it, marginals could be wrong; the code falls back to all non-constant tables only when a marginal is empty, and the snap could then force a wrong table.
Snap-to-nearest-consistent-table can override the model's written table; it changed nothing on this batch but would on a transcription error, which is the intended veto/assemble behavior.
Only 10 instances, single seed and cached solver; ambiguous end states (multiple candidates left) never occurred here, so the model's pick among remaining tables is untested.
The 'truth' word and file/os patterns are forbidden by audit.py; future edits to prompt text must avoid them.
